newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Weak gold price pressures marginal Evander.
newsitem.headline: Weak gold price pressures marginal Evander.

text.p: Evander Gold Mines Ltd's status as a marginal producer and pressure from the current weak gold price had forced the company to waive the payment of a final dividend, Gengold Ltd said on Monday.

"Evander is the most marginal of our producers. (It) is really under pressure at the current gold price and we really do need to have a good deal with our people in order to get the mine into the black," Gengold chairman Tom Dale said at the release of the the group's second quarter results.
"I really don't think it will be prudent to pay a dividend."

Second quarter distributable profit at Evander -- the resultant company formed by merging Kinross Mines Ltd, Leslie Gold Mines Ltd and Winkelhaak Ltd -- tumbled to 2.61 million rand from 32.81 million rand in the preceding quarter.

"The unified executive management structure at EGM is working well but given the current gold price, future production and cost targets for the company will depend to a large degree on progress in the current wage negotiations, which are focused on improving gold output," Gengold said.
Dale said Gengold's priority in the wage talks was to get agreement on raising productivity by working more shifts.

"We need a substantial amount of extra gold production at Evander to get it on its feet. For the September quarter, Evander's future will depend on the co-operation that we establish with the workforce," he told Reuters.
Gengold's mines worked 66 out of the possible 91 shifts available in the June quarter.

"It was a short quarter because of holidays and then there was a stayaway. There were 91 shifts in the quarter that could have been worked and we worked 66. No industry, no international commodity business can be run profitably on that basis," Dale said.
Dale said Gengold's June quarter results were "okay" but that the lower average gold price and the fewer shifts worked had taken their toll.

He said Gengold's average gold price in the June quarter was 49,000 rand/kg compared to the preceding quarter's 51,000 rand/kg. "There was quite a material decline in the average gold price," Dale said.

Asked about the recent two-year productivity-linked wage agreement between the Chamber of Mines and the National Union of Mineworkers, Dale declined to say how much Gengold planned to raise production this year to meet the industry's target of a 90 tonne increase in gold output.

"It varies from mine to mine. It's not an average. Evander is a marginal mine and Beatrix is the lowest cost producer in the industry and one of the best mines in the world. So to talk about Gengold is nonsensical," he said.
Evander said that it was trying to get commitment to improve production to above two tonnes a month. It produced 4.9 tonnes of gold in the three months to June.
